analysis: Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 847-1403). No patch hunks or head text were supplied, so the actual PR delta is not visible, and I cannot confirm what changed in this file or whether the PR changes code elsewhere. The excerpted text is release-note prose with no executable behavior. It describes already-shipped or draft controls that match the canonical threat model: App Attest authorization (A-015, A-016, A-017, TB-011, T-052..T-058), and the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035). It also mentions the 30-minute TTL, the 20 GiB write reserve, and account-scoped cache salts. Nothing here weakens or contradicts those descriptions, and no new attack surface appears. Later integration should check two things. First, whether any head-side CHANGELOG edit claims a security property that the code or threat model does not support, for example that App Attest proves unique hardware, or that the SSD cache TTL or disk-budget policy is changed without a SEC-035 sign-off. Second, whether companion code changes in the PR (coordinator, provider-swift, console-ui) are covered by other units. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied material.
